new_statements.relation_note: Catalog (StressTyp2 < Noonan 1992:42): primary stress invariably on the root vowel, first vowel of a polysyllabic root; particles/prepositions unstressed and cliticized. Tucker & Bryan's chapter-wide rule 'stress on the Stem, never on Prefixes or Suffixes' is the same root/stem-stress type; it is less specific (says nothing about which stem syllable) and adds only the remark that stress and vowel length are related in S. Lwo. No contradiction.
new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Nilotic languages treated (Dinka, Nuer, N. Lwo = Shilluk, S. Lwo = Acoli-Lango, Alur, Kenya Luo) stress falls on the stem of the word and never on prefixes or suffixes; in S. Lwo (which includes Lango) stress appears to be connected with vowel length. No statement recovered about which syllable of a polysyllabic stem is stressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Prefixes and suffixes are never stressed; 'some relationship between stress and vowel length in S. LWO' (cross-ref § 14 (i), not recovered); Acoli-Lango has only two degrees of vowel length, truly long vowels mostly in final open syllables. The statement is a chapter-wide 'general rule', not Lango-specific.
new_statements.identity_note: Tucker & Bryan treat Lango jointly with Acoli as 'ACOLI-LANGO', the exemplar of the S. LWO head of ch. 30 'The Nilotic Languages' (informant list includes 'N. E. Opio, LANGO, ACOLI'); the stress rule is stated once for the whole chapter (Dinka, Nuer, N. Lwo, S. Lwo), not for Lango alone. The catalog record rests on Noonan 1992 (Lango of Lira district, Uganda).

sources.note: Per Clifton 1975 (copy consulted read, secs. 1-2): 'MSO' proposed two tone rules for Lango, Tone Shift and Tone Copy, stated over high, low and falling tones on vowels, to account for tonal alternations in noun paradigms and phrases; Clifton re-analyses some of their forms with floating ('nonsegmental') H tones. Bennett 1974 cites it in a discussion concluding that tonal case marking is lacking in the Luo group.

tone.n_tones: 2 levels (H, L) plus falling contour, per Clifton's restatement of the MSO rules
